speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many companies in Singapore currently practise some form of a shorter work week; and (b) whether assistance and guidance can be provided for companies considering to implement shorter work weeks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In such arrangements, the employee does not need to contemplate reducing his income in exchange for greater flexibility in work days, since the actual workload and total hours worked in a week do not differ from that of a person on a standard work week.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It is useful to remember that flexible work arrangements are not limited only to remote work or hybrid work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The concept of a compressed work week is a form of flexible work arrangement that is suitable for certain jobs and some employees, but not all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In promoting workplace flexibility, we encourage companies to implement the type of flexible work arrangement that best suits their business and their employees.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can MOM further recognise HR best practices, such as shorter work weeks and flexible work arrangements?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Also, to what extent are HR practices a factor in tender specifications, for instance, either as a tie breaker or hygiene factor?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to ensure that good HR practices are further recognised in Government tenders and procurement processes?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: It is in our interest to recognise companies with good workplace practices that are progressive.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: For recognition of progressive workplaces and progressive employers, we do have other ways to recognise them as well.
